title: Conversation Telemetry Signal Map — Journal
body:
Purpose
--------
Personal notebook for converging on a canonical signal map for conversation-level telemetry. This is a sketch-first brain dump: API shapes, sampling notes, enrichment rules, privacy constraints, and a small ASCII diagram of where signals are emitted. Aim is to have a compact, operationally useful set of events we can wire into Console tracing, Optimize evals, and alerting.

Goals (high level)
- Define a small-footprint event schema that captures decision points (routing, cache hit/miss, batch boundaries) without blowing up event cardinality.
- Provide consistent keys that product, SRE, and ML can rely on for aggregations and SLIs.
- Ensure PII-safe defaults and clear redaction/enrichment rules.
- Define sampling & downsampling so long tails don't flood our ingestion.

Key concepts / vocabulary
- conversation_id: stable id for UX-level convo (user-visible). Not tenant-specific.
- session_id: ephemeral session (client connection) — may span multiple conversations.
- request_id: one API call (ingress to final token emitted). Unique per call.
- probe_id: lightweight per-host/per-runtime stamp to help group events in traces.
- model_variant: canonical model name + quantization suffix (e.g., llama-2-13b-q4f32).
- route: policy that routed this request (e.g., latency-preferred, cost-fallback).
- prefix_cache_key: hashed short key for prefix KV cache. Not raw prompt.

Foundational signals (emit at these points)
1) ingress.receive (when request hits front-door)
   required fields: request_id, tenant_id, client_id, timestamp, route, conversation_id?, session_id?, request_size_tokens_est
   notes: don't store raw prompt. store prompt_hash and prompt_length.

2) ingress.authz (auth decision)
   fields: request_id, decision (allow|deny), auth_method, policy_id, latency_ms

3) routing.decision
   fields: request_id, route, candidates_checked (list-of-strings — store up to 3), reason_codes (comma-list), routing_latency_ms

4) cache.prefix_lookup
   fields: request_id, prefix_cache_key, hit (true|false), cache_latency_ms, cache_ttl_bucket

5) batch.window (if request batched)
   fields: request_id, batch_id, batch_size, batch_wait_ms

6) runtime.model_infer.start and .end
   fields: request_id, model_variant, seq_in, seq_out, tokens_generated, infer_ms, quant_profile

7) postprocess.safe_filter / moderation
   fields: request_id, moderation_flag (none|sensitive|blocked), filter_latency_ms

8) emit.response (when response leaves system)
   fields: request_id, status (ok|error|degraded), total_time_ms, tokens_sent, priced_token_bucket

Signal cardinality & event size constraints
- Keep each event < 1 KB by default. Avoid including long strings.
- Use hashed identifiers for user content (prompt_hash, embed_hash).
- Limit variable-length arrays: candidates_checked up to 3, reason_codes up to 5.
- For heavy telemetry (complete prompt trace) gate behind an explicit opt-in and put on a separate retention tier.

PII & privacy rules
- Never include raw prompt text in standard telemetry. Use prompt_hash (sha256 hex) and prompt_length_tokens (int).
- Redact any extracted entities before telemetry: e.g., named entities heuristics should be scrubbed unless tenant has consented and workspace-level setting enabled.
- IPs and device ids: only hashed (sha256) at ingestion; store provenance flags instead of raw addresses.
- Put a feature-flag: telemetry.full_context.enabled -> when false, ingress.receive must drop any context payloads and set context_redacted=true.

Sampling policy (fast first pass)
- Deterministic reservoir by tenant: sample_k_per_min_per_tenant default 50 for heavy transports to keep per-tenant skyline stable.
- Trace sampling for distributed traces: sample 1 in 10 full traces, but emit lightweight summary for 100% of requests.
- Tail sampling: keep 100% of requests that exceed latency SLO or trigger error. Implement in router/collector shorthand.

Backfill & enrichment
- Enrichment pipeline (async) will add: model-serving-node, gpu_type, quant_profile, contiguous_error_count (recent), eval_prompt_tag.
- Backfilled fields must be nullable in downstream tables. Don’t rely on enrichment for SLIs that must be realtime.

Canonical event schema (flat key list)
- event_type (string)
- timestamp (ISO)
- request_id (string)
- conversation_id (string, optional)
- session_id (string, optional)
- tenant_id (string)
- route (string)
- model_variant (string, optional)
- prompt_hash (string, optional)
- prompt_length_tokens (int, optional)
- tokens_generated (int, optional)
- infer_ms (int, optional)
- batch_id (string, optional)
- batch_size (int, optional)
- cache_hit (bool, optional)
- moderation_flag (string, optional)
- status (string)
- sample_rate_hint (float)  // 1.0 means full, 0.1 means 10% stored

Example minimal event (as telemetry line)
- ingress.receive | {timestamp: 2026-02-17T14:42:05Z, request_id: r_9a3f, tenant_id: t_acme, route: latency-preferred, prompt_hash: 3b6f..., prompt_length_tokens: 42, sample_rate_hint: 1.0}

Instrumentation hooks (where to wire)
- SDK / client: stamp session_id, conversation_id, client_features; client should send only prompt_hash unless debug enabled.
- Edge ingress: compute prompt_hash, perform initial policy checks, emit ingress.receive + authz events.
- Router: emit routing.decision and sampling hint. Router may short-circuit and emit emit.response when policy denies.
- Runtime: kernel-level spans around model inference and KV cache lookups. Emit cache.prefix_lookup and runtime.model_infer.start/end.
- Postprocess: moderation + tool-calls instrumentation. Track any blocking filters as separate events.

ASCII diagram (very rough)
- client -> edge-ingress -> router -> runtime-pool -> postprocess -> response
         |            |            |
         v            v            v
      telemetry     cache svc    metrics collector

Operational use-cases (quick wins)
- SLO alert: p95 total_time_ms by route and model_variant. Keep p95 ingest->emit as default.
- Cache impact: measure tokens_saved_estimated by prefix cache hit rate aggregated per prompt_hash_prefix_bucket per day.
- Cost vs quality guardrail: correlate route (cost-fallback) with eval-quality scores (from Optimize) using prompt_hash join.

Edge cases & open questions
- How to represent multi-turn partial responses where user aborts mid-stream? proposal: emit an abort_reason on emit.response and tokens_sent=actual.
- Session affinity churn: we need a TTL for session_id reuse to avoid explosion across mobile app restarts. Recommend 24h TTL unless client-provided persistent session.
- Model variant aliases: allow mapping table (alias -> canonical) in enrichment stage to prevent metric splits.

Next steps (for me)
- Iterate on event definitions with Liam and SRE; produce a thin proto/avro and a short ingestion contract.
- Prototype a small sampling shim in router to tag sample_rate_hint.
- Add a Console dashboard template: p95/median total_time, cache hit rate, rate of moderation flags by tenant.

Notes to self
- Keep telemetry lightweight by default — teams will always ask for more fields, but default must be safe & small.
- Put full-context tracing behind opt-in plus longer retention, separate billing.
- Cross-check with legal on prompt_hash being acceptable as non-PII for our regions.

References and links
- Confluence: CONF-telemetry-landingpage-4821 (linked above)
- JIRA: JIRA-OPS-1892 (routing sampling ticket)

TODO
- [ ] draft avro schema from canonical key list
- [ ] run a 1-week sampling sim against synthetic workload to estimate total ingestion
- [ ] sync with privacy/legal on prompt_hash policy
- [ ] quic-kv metric to surface prefix_cache_key cardinality

End of page.
